name: Wren (wren-review01)

findings.title: providers.result labels a recovered error followed by terminal success as quota
findings.trace: Docstring says stderr-triggered cooldown only after nonzero exit, but code appends every error/turn.failed/run.terminal.failed event to error_text regardless of exit_code or terminal. Quota regex is then applied unconditionally and quota wins over success.
findings.reproduction: Executed: result('codex', '{"type":"error","message":"rate limit reached but retried"}\n{"type":"turn.completed","usage":{"input_tokens":10,"output_tokens":2}}', '', 0) -> {'outcome':'quota', ...}. The run succeeded with a terminal event, yet is classified as quota and would receive the 15-minute quota cooldown instead of success. Existing test test_tool_quoted_limit_is_not_quota_and_usage_is_not_invented only covers tool text in item.completed, not a prior JSON error event.

findings.title: providers.result misses real quota reported in non-JSON stdout or dropped by 16KB tail truncation
findings.trace: Non-JSON stdout lines are skipped (continue), so plain-text quota output never enters error_text. If exit_code is nonzero, only errors[-16000:] is searched; an early quota line followed by more than 16KB of diagnostics is lost.
findings.reproduction: Executed: result('codex', 'quota exhausted', '', 1) -> {'outcome':'failed'} and result('codex', '', 'quota exhausted\n'+'x'*20000, 1) -> {'outcome':'failed'}. A truly quota-exhausted provider is thus recorded as failed, gets the shorter failed cooldown, and may be retried sooner/other providers may be exhausted in turn.

findings.title: life run-finish does not release the dead resident's live task leases
findings.category: strand quota-exhausted residents / lose concurrent work
findings.trace: run-finish sets the resident awake=false and requeues help_requests on non-success, but never releases or reopens tasks owned by that run resident. Model claim at house/model.py:91 requires until <= at, so a task claimed for up to 86400s (lease ceiling) by a quota/interrupted/failed run remains blocked for the whole TTL even though another provider kind with quota could do it.
findings.reproduction: Logical trace: claim task with seconds=1800; run-finish outcome=quota. life state shows task still status=claimed, owner=dead resident, until in future. Next resident claim(..., expect=generation+1) is rejected as 'task has a live lease'. No supervisor release path exists in life.apply for quota/interrupted/failed. Tests cover help requeue but not task-lease release.

findings.title: integrate allows self-review and self-publish of the same run
findings.category: bypass cooperative/Steward review boundary through normal tool
findings.trace: integrate only requires actor in residents (line 32). It never checks actor != run resident, different kind, or independence from the contribution author. The same actor who authored the workspace can call integrate(..., publish=True) and satisfy the 'reviewed' gate with only the automated test run.
findings.reproduction: Logical trace: actor == life.runs[run]['resident'] passes line 32; line 61-68 publishes if tests pass. Owner objective requires a different-kind independent witness; AGENTS.md says the integrating resident reviews, implying non-authorship. Inspection found no tests at all for integrate.py covering independence.

findings.title: inbox poll aborts the whole poll on one malformed owner issue/comment
findings.category: strand owner wake requests / lose concurrent work
findings.trace: After the owner filter, requests() raises ValueError if id is not int or body is not str. poll() iterates requests() before appending anything, so a single owner item with body:null (valid GitHub empty body) aborts the entire poll. The cursor is then never advanced, so every later poll refetches the same 60s-overlap window and fails again, blocking all later valid owner wake requests.
findings.reproduction: Logical trace: requests([], [{'id':10,'user':{'id':OWNER_ID},'body':None,'html_url':'...'}]) raises 'malformed owner issue'. Poll catches nothing, writes only inbox-error (coordinator side), appends no help and no cursor receipt. tests/test_inbox.py covers owner filter/notice exclusion but has no null-body case.

strengths: life.py journal-serialized capacity, budget gating, help single-take, ambition CAS, and run single-launch checks operate atomically under Record.locked (house/life.py:97-112, 141-152; test_capacity_is_journal_enforced, test_concurrent_process_admission_cannot_exceed_three).

resident_client pins canonical repo, resident actor, and artifacts-from, rejects --repo override and controller-only life kinds (house/resident_client.py:22-33), covered by test_fixed_client_rejects_other_actor_and_global_repo_override.

providers.validate_model enforces the finite Steward allowlist and command() drops API-key env, sandboxes agy/muse, and denies opencode shell/external_directory except the fixed client (house/providers.py:26-72).

inbox.requests is owner-only, excludes PRs/control issue/emoji-notice/VETO/REPEAL, and uses idempotent request IDs with body digest edits creating new work but re-polls replaying (house/inbox.py:28-45, tests/test_inbox.py).

integrate never resets/stashes/overwrites the shared checkout; it merges in a private clone, runs tests, rechecks clean HEAD before ff-only publish, and retains conflict/tests-failed candidates (house/integrate.py:40-73).

runtime selection verifies directory/name/symlink/hash and bootstraps only from steward-authorized source with protected manifest checks (house/runtime.py:20-28, 43-53), covered by tests/test_runtime.py.
uncertainties: OpenCode bash pattern 'client *' (house/providers.py:58-62) against shell-operator chaining and argparse last-wins --repo: not exercised against a live opencode binary here; left as uncertainty, not a finding.
Whether repeated turn.completed/step_finish events are cumulative totals (sum is correct) vs repeated snapshots (sum would double-count): needs live provider fixtures per kind.
Actual cooldown durations, quiet backoff, coordinator uptime, and lease TTL impact under real quota cadence were not exercised; no live model wakes attempted.
house/home.py excluded per instructions; lease handoff, cooldown call sites, and coordinator capacity logic there were read only for context and not cited as findings.
